public_body: Everett School Committee On Finance And Negotiation
overall: The AG found a violation because the subcommittee's six executive session notices for union negotiations did not name the bargaining unit, and ordered future compliance; the general purpose description was held sufficient.

allegations.summary: Six executive session notices (April–July 2021) allegedly gave insufficient detail about the executive sessions held to negotiate with union personnel.
allegations.key_passage: by failing to identify as part of each executive session notice item the collective bargaining unit with which the Subcommittee would be negotiating

allegations.summary: Notices combined Purpose 2 and Purpose 3 wording and cited only one statute, which was challenged as too vague to show the sessions were proper.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Subcommittee provided enough description to make clear that the six executive sessions would all concern topics that were appropriate for executive session

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a future similar violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
remedy_passage: We order the Subcommittee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Subcommittee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
